meta.title: Vellum | Maps for cities worth remembering
meta.description: Vellum turns Cities: Skylines 1 .cslmap exports into layered maps you can explore, theme, and export as PNG or editable SVG.
meta.ogDescription: Open a Cities: Skylines 1 .cslmap export and read your city in layers.

hero.eyebrow: A cartographic viewer for Cities: Skylines 1
hero.title: A map for the city you built.
hero.ledeAfter: export and read your city in layers.
hero.imageAlt: Spring Valley map in Vellum Day theme, showing a broad city between rivers and coast

promise.title: Your city should be readable outside the game.
promise.body: Vellum turns a Cities: Skylines export into a map you can inspect, share, and preserve.

cities.title: The shape of a city is already a story.
cities.body: These are Cities: Skylines maps opened in Vellum, with their original Workshop sources kept in view.

layers.title: See the city become legible.
layers.body: Start with terrain and base map, then bring roads, buildings, forests, districts, and transit into the reading.

transit.title: Follow the network.
transit.body: Inspect lines and stops over the city they serve, then use the minimap to stay oriented as you move through the view.
transit.note: When transit is the story, the map can make it the subject.

themes.futureTitle: Create a visual language of your own.
themes.futureBody: A custom .vellumstyle format is planned. Its schema is still being formalized for community-made themes.

workflow.title: From export to artifact.
workflow.body: Vellum sits after the game and before the work you want to keep.
workflow.openBody: Pan, zoom, inspect transit, control the layers, and keep your bearings with the minimap.
workflow.exportBody: Save a PNG for sharing or an editable SVG for the next pass.

openSource.title: Open by design.
openSource.body: Vellum is open source under the MIT License. Read the code, follow the documentation, and see how the map is made.
